terms.gloss: a document, a deed; in the plural, the papers of a case or a business
evidence: Suet. Calig. 8: pūblicī īnstrūmentī auctōritās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of writings, an instrument, document or record (Lewis & Short): post-Augustan prose and the jurists. Otherwise īnstrūmentum is a tool or equipment, so the context must show the sense.

terms.gloss: written records: accounts, registers, a will
evidence: Cic. Arch. 8: tabulae pūblicae, the public records (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s word for documents kept on record, from the writing-tablets they were written on.

terms.gloss: an official document granting a privilege
terms.comment: A letter folded double: a state warrant or passport for travel, later any document by which a magistrate granted a favour (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a lesson, an example, a warning; a proof
terms.comment: A false friend for a paper document: classically what teaches, a lesson or a warning (Lewis & Short). Traupman keeps it for a file on a computer (see document, on a computer).

phrases.latin: ideōque opus est intuērī omne lītis īnstrūmentum; quod vidēre nōn est satis, perlegendum erit.
phrases.english: So you must look over all the documents of the case: seeing them is not enough, they must be read through.

sources: Lewis & Short: instrumentum · Lewis & Short: tabula · Lewis & Short: diploma · Lewis & Short: documentum
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. document: official document.
